extracted.intended_audience: applicants and practitioners preparing or prosecuting PCT (international) patent applications via the United States Receiving Office (USPTO); patent agents/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures for preparing, filing, and processing an international (PCT) patent application at the United States Receiving Office, including formal contents, fees, priority, unity, amendments, representation, and related timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall contain, as specified in the Treaty and the Regulations, a Request, a description, one or more claims, an abstract, and one or more drawings (where required). (PCT Art. 3(2) and Section 207 of the Administrative Instructions.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parts must conform to PCT requirements; drawings only when required for understanding. See related sections for form/content specifics (Request, description, claims, abstract, drawings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office accord of international filing date — US resident/national
rubrics_metrics.description: An international filing date will be accorded by the United States Receiving Office provided that at least one applicant is a United States resident or national and the papers filed at the time of receipt of the international application so indicate (35 U.S.C. 361(a), PCT Art. 11(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applicant residency/nationality is clearly indicated on filing papers to obtain an international filing date from the US RO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application is in the English language (35 U.S.C. 361(c), PCT Art. 11(1)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed in another language will not meet this US RO requirement; translations may be necessary per PCT rules and Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum elements required on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must contain at least: (i) an indication that it is intended as an international application (PCT Rule 4.2); (ii) the designation of at least one Contracting State of the International Patent Cooperation Union (§ 1.432); (iii) the name of the applicant, as prescribed; (iv) a part which on the face of it appears to be a description; and (v) a part which on the face of it appears to be a claim. (PCT Art. 11(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimal elements suffice to obtain an international filing date; include clear parts so they visibly resemble a description and a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing for international/transmittal/search fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the international filing fee (PCT Rule 15.2) and the transmittal and search fees may be made in full at the time the international application papers are deposited or within one month thereafter. The fees payable are those in effect on the receipt date of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees are not paid within one month, procedures for notice and late payment apply (see late payment fee rules). Fee amounts depend on receipt date and entity status (micro/small/other).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment fee calculation and cap
rubrics_metrics.description: If deficient fees are not paid within one month and prior to sending of a notice imposing a late payment fee, applicant gets one month to pay the deficient fees plus the late payment fee. The late payment fee will be equal to the greater of: (i) fifty percent of the amount of the deficient fees; or (ii) an amount equal to the transmittal fee. The late payment fee shall not exceed an amount equal to fifty percent of the international filing fee (excluding any fee for sheets in excess of thirty). (PCT Rule 16bis.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-month time limit to cure deficient fees may not be extended. Failure to timely pay per PCT Rule 16bis.1(e) leads to declaration of withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal for failure to pay required fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If payment needed to cover the transmittal fee, the international filing fee, the search fee, and the late payment fee is not timely made in accordance with PCT Rule 16bis.1(e), the Receiving Office will declare the international application withdrawn under PCT Article 14(3)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment is essential to avoid automatic withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of States by filing an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing the international application request constitutes: (a) designation of all Contracting States bound by the Treaty on the international filing date; (b) indication that the application is, for each designated State to which PCT Articles 43 or 44 apply, for the grant of every kind of protection available by designation of that State; and (c) indication that for each State to which PCT Article 45(1) applies the application is for grant of a regional patent and, unless Article 45(2) applies, also a national patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single filing effectually designates many downstream rights — ensure desired states are covered and understand regional vs national grant options under PCT Articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application and each document referred to in the Request shall be filed in one copy only. All sheets of the international application must be on A4 size paper (21.0 x 29.7 cm.). Other physical requirements are set forth in PCT Rule 11 and Administrative Instructions sections 201-207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PCT Rule 11 and Administrative Instructions for margins, paper, numbering, etc.; nonconforming physical format may cause processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request form and Check List requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall be made on a standardized form (PCT Rules 3 and 4). The Check List portion should indicate each document accompanying the international application on filing. All information (addresses, names of States, dates) shall be indicated as required by PCT Rule 4 and Administrative Instructions 110 and 201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official Request/Demand forms; ensure the Check List accurately lists all accompanying documents to avoid omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request content for designation of the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: For designation of the United States of America, an international application shall include: (1) the name of the inventor; and (2) a reference to any prior-filed national application or international application designating the United States of America, if the benefit of the filing date for the prior-filed application is to be claimed. An international application may also include in the Request a declaration of the inventors as provided for in PCT Rule 4.17(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inventor names and priority references on the Request when claiming benefit of earlier U.S. filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description content and best mode requirement (US designation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must meet the requirements as to the content and form of the description set forth in PCT Rules 5, 9, 10, and 11 and Administrative Instructions sections 204 and 208. In international applications designating the United States the description must contain upon filing an indication of the best mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with PCT content/form rules. For US designation, disclose the best mode on filing to meet the US-specific requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims content, format, and reasonable number
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements as to the content and format of claims are set forth in PCT Art. 6 and PCT Rules 6, 9, 10 and 11 and shall be adhered to. The number of the claims shall be reasonable, considering the nature of the invention claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims to satisfy PCT formal requirements and avoid excessive claim counts relative to the invention's nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required when they are necessary for the understanding of the invention (PCT Art. 7). The physical requirements for drawings are set forth in PCT Rule 11 and shall be adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include drawings when needed to understand the invention; prepare drawings to PCT physical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and charge types for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees and charges established include a transmittal fee (basic portion with tiers by entity status and receipt date), an international filing fee (PCT Rule 15), a search fee, supplemental search fees (per additional invention), a fee equivalent to the transmittal fee if USPTO acted as Receiving Office for IB processing, late furnishing fee for sequence listings, and a late payment fee pursuant to PCT Rule 16bis.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amounts vary by receipt date and applicant entity status (micro/small/other). Refer to the specific tables and the PCT Rules for exact fees applicable to a given receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of international application fees — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Money paid for international application fees, where paid by actual mistake or in excess (such as a payment not required by law or treaty and its regulations), may be refunded. A mere change of purpose after the payment of a fee will not entitle a party to a refund of such fee. The Office will not refund amounts of twenty-five dollars or less unless a refund is specifically requested and will not notify the payor of such amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File refund requests promptly and provide banking info for EFT refunds; requests must be filed within two years for most refunds (see §1.446(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund conditions and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for refund must be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid. If the Office charges a deposit account by an amount other than specifically indicated, refund requests based on such charge must be filed within two years from the deposit account statement date and include a copy of that statement. Time periods are not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve payment records and act within two years for refund claims; include necessary documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific refundable fees and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Refund of supplemental search fees may be made if determined warranted by the Director under PCT Rule 40.2(c). International and search fees will be refunded if no international filing date is accorded or if application withdrawn before transmittal of the record copy to the International Bureau; the search fee will be refunded if withdrawn before transmittal of the search copy to the International Searching Authority. The transmittal fee will not be refunded. The handling fee will be refunded only if the Demand is withdrawn before it has been sent to the International Bureau or the Demand is considered not submitted (PCT Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of withdrawal/transmittal determines refund eligibility; transmittal fee generally non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim form and certified copy procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority must be made on the Request in a manner complying with Administrative Instructions sections 110 and 115 (PCT Rule 4.10). When priority of an earlier US application is claimed, the applicant may request that the USPTO prepare a certified copy of the prior application for transmittal to the International Bureau (PCT Article 8 and PCT Rule 17); the fee is set forth in §1.19(b)(1). If the certified copy is not submitted on filing or requested with payment, the certified copy must be furnished within the time limit in PCT Rule 17.1(a). The applicant may correct or add a priority claim in accordance with PCT Rule 26bis.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make priority claims on the Request and either submit certified copies or request USPTO certification within the allowed time to avoid delay in processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority (unintentional delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international filing date is later than the expiration of the priority period but within two months from that expiration, the right of priority may be restored upon request if the delay in filing was unintentional. The request must be filed not later than two months from the expiration of the priority period and must include a notice adding the priority claim if not contained, the petition fee (§1.17(m)), and a statement that the delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is available only for unintentional delays within the two-month window and requires fee and supporting statements; early publication requests can affect timing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of earlier search/classification results
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant requests that an International Searching Authority take into account results of an earlier search, the United States Receiving Office shall prepare and transmit copies of results and any earlier classification as provided under PCT Rules 23bis.1 and 23bis.2, subject to confidentiality exceptions. The US RO will not prepare/transmit results from an application preserved in confidence unless written authority granting access is provided and signed by an appropriate person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide written authority when earlier search results are in an application preserved in confidence; request transmittal on filing or submit authority promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and appointment of agents/attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may be represented by attorneys or agents registered to practice before the USPTO or by an applicant appointed as a common representative (PCT Art. 49, Rules 4.8 and 90, §11.9). If no representative is appointed and there is more than one applicant, the first named applicant entitled to file at the US RO is considered the common representative. Appointment must be effected in the Request form, Demand form, or separate power of attorney submitted to the US RO or IB. Powers of attorney and revocations should be submitted to the US RO until issuance of the international search report. An attorney or agent may appoint an associate who will then be of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit clear appointment documents on the prescribed forms; appointments revoke earlier appointments unless indicated otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of record copy to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal of the record copy to the International Bureau shall be made by the United States Receiving Office as provided by PCT Rule 19.4. No copy of an international application may be transmitted to the International Bureau, a foreign Designated Office, or other foreign authority by the US RO or applicant unless the applicable requirements of part 5 of this chapter have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all part 5 requirements are met before expecting transmittal to IB or foreign designated offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of application processing based on priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: For computing time limits under the Treaty, the priority date is defined as in PCT Art. 2(xi). Corrections, additions, withdrawals of priority claims affect the priority date for computing non-expired time limits: the priority date will be the filing date of the earliest remaining priority claim or, if none, the international filing date. When certain corrections are timely submitted but received later than one year from the claimed priority date(s), the Receiving Office shall proceed under PCT Rule 26bis.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor how changes to priority claims affect deadlines; use the correct effective priority date when calculating time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse for delays in meeting time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays in meeting time limits during international processing of international applications may only be excused as provided in PCT Rule 82. For delays in national applications see §1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief is only available under the limited circumstances in PCT Rule 82; plan to meet deadlines or seek authorized extensions where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and amendments during international processing
rubrics_metrics.description: All corrections submitted to the US RO or US ISA must be in English, in the form of replacement sheets in compliance with PCT Rules 10 and 11, and accompanied by a letter drawing attention to differences between replaced and replacement sheets. Replacement sheets are not required for deletion of lines, correction of simple typographical errors, and one addition/change of not more than five words per sheet; such minor changes may be stated in a letter and, if appropriate, the US RO will make the deletion or transfer the correction provided such corrections do not adversely affect clarity and direct reproducibility. Amendments not complying with PCT Rules 10 and 11.1–11.13 may not be entered. Amendments of claims submitted to the IB shall be as prescribed by PCT Rule 46. Corrections/additions to the Request or declarations under PCT Rule 4.17 should be submitted to the IB as prescribed by PCT Rule 26ter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use replacement sheets for substantive corrections; minor typographical adjustments can be handled by letter subject to clarity constraints; nonconforming amendments will be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in person, name, or address of applicants/inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for change in person, name or address of applicants and inventors should be sent to the United States Receiving Office until issuance of the international search report; thereafter requests should be submitted to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit such changes to the correct office depending on processing stage to ensure they are recorded timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An international and a national stage application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. Unity is fulfilled only when there is a technical relationship among the inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. 'Special technical features' are those that define a contribution which each claimed invention makes over the prior art. Combinations of categories that are accepted as having unity are limited to specific enumerated groupings (e.g., product + process specially adapted to manufacture that product; process + apparatus designed to carry out the process; product + process of use of product; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims and claim sets to demonstrate a single general inventive concept or to fall within the permitted category combinations; otherwise lack of unity objections and additional fees may follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unity by the International Searching Authority and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Before establishing the international search report, the ISA will determine whether the application complies with the unity requirement. If ISA considers application lacks unity it shall inform the applicant and invite payment of additional fees (PCT Art.17 and Rule 40). The applicant is given a time period per PCT Rule 40.3 to pay additional fees. If no additional fees are paid, the international search will be performed only on the invention first mentioned ('main invention') in the claims. Lack of unity may be evident before considering the claims in relation to prior art or after taking prior art into account; ISA may raise the objection when prior art shows lack of common inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate possible unity objections; consider structuring claims or being prepared to pay additional search fees or protest the objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure against lack of unity and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with a lack-of-unity holding by the ISA, additional fees may be paid under protest accompanied by a request for refund and a statement of reasons (PCT Rule 40.2(c)). The protest will be examined by the Director or designee; if determined justified, additional fees or a portion will be refunded. The applicant may request that a copy of the protest and the decision accompany the international search report when forwarded to Designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the protest procedure to preserve rights and seek refunds where the ISA's lack-of-unity finding is believed incorrect; file the protest timely and include explanatory reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for international preliminary examination — form and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: On the filing of a proper Demand in an application for which the US International Preliminary Examining Authority is competent and for which the fees have been paid, the international application shall be the subject of an international preliminary examination. The preliminary examination fee (§1.482(a)(1)) and the handling fee (§1.482(b)) shall be due within the applicable time limit set forth in PCT Rule 57.3. The Demand shall be made on a standardized form (PCT Rule 53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the Demand on the official form and pay required fees within the PCT Rule 57.3 time limits to obtain international preliminary examination by the US IPEA.
